title: A warehouse timetable
bodyMd:
A fictional city proposed converting a warehouse into a performance venue. The structure appeared sound, and campaigners emphasized that reuse could retain the building’s identity. A feasibility study, however, found that the proposed evening events would overlap with loading operations in the adjoining market. The conflict concerned shared access routes rather than the warehouse’s physical capacity.

The planners revised the schedule and created a separate pedestrian entrance. They argued that adaptability involves more than fitting a new activity inside old walls. Buildings participate in surrounding patterns of movement, work and time. A reuse scheme can preserve a shell yet fail if it ignores those relations. The revised project therefore treated operating hours and access arrangements as design decisions alongside structural repairs.
